alternatives.argument: Move the oriented knot off infinity to R3. Under AComega, choose a regular projection. The local disk-and-band correctness proof gives a connected compact oriented embedded surface with exactly the represented knot as boundary; pull it back by the inverse ambient isotopy.

Define the surface as a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface in standard S3 with the boundary orientation equal to the knot. Under AComega, the finite-chart surface normal-form item supplies the unique genus integer through chi=2-2g-b.

The local existence theorem makes the subset of natural numbers represented by genera of admissible surfaces nonempty. The well-ordering principle gives a least element, which is the smooth knot genus.

Remove two interior disks from an unknot disk and attach an unknotted annular tube. Finite cell counts give chi=-1 and b=1, so the resulting surface has genus 1. The original disk has genus 0; hence the knot genus is 0 and the constructed surface is not minimal.

alternatives.argument: For each crossing perform the unique orientation-compatible smoothing; record the resulting finite Seifert circles; choose separated disk heights; attach one orientation-matched half-twisted band per crossing; return the finite disk-and-band data and counts.

The smoothed circles bound disk regions under AComega and simple connectivity of S2. Nesting assigns distinct heights. In disjoint crossing neighborhoods, raise compatible attaching collars above ancestor disks and attach one half-twisted rectangle matching the over-under crossing. The local boundary is the original knot; every component retains an unbanded boundary arc, so the one boundary circle forces connectedness.

Move an oriented knot into R3, choose a regular projection using the AComega regular-projection lemma, apply the local disk-band realization, and pull the resulting surface back by the inverse ambient isotopy.
